title: 只能选两样：从来不及、会忘记到说不清——六个核心，看懂复杂世界的取舍 / Pick Two: Six Ideas for Understanding a Complicated World
description:
中文. 本著作是这一系列的入口读本：用六个核心，把六本学术专著写成一本从十岁到专家都能读完的书。

核心主张：看得见的世界背后有一张看不见的账单，账单只有三个价格——看得准、拼得上、传得下去，最多付得起两个。六个核心（看见、记住、跟上、选择、讲述、临界）就是学会读这六张账单。

结构与证据：19 部、123 页、29 幅图；四种读者分层（故事／多想一层／再想一层／给专家的注），每部配三个生活故事与动手练习，另有练习册、常见误解、给老师家长的一页与二十五个真实的人。

诚实的纪律：每个核心都标明对应专著的证据等级；凡通俗化损伤原意之处，以专著为准；本书不新增实证结论。

边界：它是入口，不是替代；具体结论与失败记录在六本专著中。它同时是系列的外部登记库（最小可验证单元、跨域盲测登记、合并术语表）。

版本：2026-10-18，123 页，19 部，29 图；源码开源，内容 CC BY 4.0，代码 MIT。

本版更新（2026-10-18 地基版）。本版把全书的共同前提写到卷首：现实中不存在无限——无限只作为极限出现在模型里，从不出现在现实系统的实际状态里。有限性本身只说明“有上界”；它要变成“必须让出一样”，还需要三个条件同时成立：需求随规模增长、描述/组合/传递共享同一承载者、同时维持两种活动更贵（交互惩罚 ψ>0）。因此“至多取二”一律是“紧预算（K/D 有界）下至多取二”的简写；若预算增长快于需求，三项可以同时满格。

本版新增内容。序章、六个核心一页速查、零基础读法与书末互引页的核心口号统一为“紧预算下，最多付得起两个”；README 与《系列速读》新增“共同地基：有限性”一节，说明有限性是必要前提而非充分条件。

系列 / Series. 同一作者的独立研究系列：六本学术专著 + 两本通俗读本。入口与外部登记库：https://github.com/lyp0746/knowledge-tradeoffs；源码与可复算脚本：https://github.com/lyp0746/knowledge-tradeoffs。首选预览文件：knowledge-tradeoffs-print.pdf（印刷版）。

English. Abstract (English). This is the entry volume of the series: six core ideas turn six monographs into a book readable from age ten to specialist. Core thesis: behind the visible world lies an invisible bill with three prices — being precise, fitting together, and carrying over — and at most two can be paid; the six cores (seeing, remembering, keeping up, choosing, telling, criticality) teach how to read that bill. Structure and evidence: 19 parts, 123 pages, 29 figures; four reader levels (story / one layer deeper / one more / expert note), three short stories and a hands-on exercise per part, plus a workbook, common misconceptions, a page for teachers and parents, and twenty-five real people. Discipline: each core points to the evidence grade of its source monograph; where popularisation distorts the original, the monograph prevails; the book adds no new empirical claims. Boundaries: it is an entry point, not a substitute; it also serves as the series' external registry. Edition: 2026-10-18, 123 pages, 19 parts, 29 figures.

What is new in this edition (2026-10-18, Finitude Edition). The common premise is now stated at the front: there is no infinity in reality — infinity appears only as a limit in models, never as a property of a real system. Finitude alone only says that there is a ceiling; to yield a trade-off it also needs three conditions: demand grows with scale, description/composition/transfer share one bearer, and maintaining two activities at once is more expensive (interaction penalty ψ>0). “At most two” is therefore shorthand for “at most two under a tight budget (bounded K/D)”; if the budget grows faster than demand, all three can be full.

New in this edition. The opening, the six-core quick reference, the zero-formula reading and the series cross-reference now say “under a tight budget, at most two”; the README and the series reader add a section on the common foundation: finitude is necessary, not sufficient.
